import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 996

*Reference:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/996](https://www.erdosproblems.com/996)
 - [Er49d] Erdös, P. "On the strong law of large numbers." Transactions of the American Mathematical
    Society 67.1 (1949): 51-56.
 - [Ma66] Matsuyama, Noboru. "On the strong law of large numbers." Tohoku Mathematical Journal,
    Second Series 18.3 (1966): 259-269.
-/

open MeasureTheory AddCircle Filter Topology Asymptotics Finset Real

namespace Erdos996

noncomputable def fourierPartial {T : ℝ} [hT : Fact (0 < T)] (f : Lp ℂ 2 (@haarAddCircle T hT))
    (k : ℕ) : AddCircle T → ℂ :=
  fun x => ∑ i ∈ Icc (-k : ℤ) k, fourierCoeff f i • fourier i x

/-- Does there exists a positive constant `C` such that for all `f ∈ L²[0,1]` and all lacunary
sequences `n`, if `‖f - fₖ‖₂ = O(1 / log log log k ^ C)`, then for almost every `x`,
`lim ∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, f (n k • x)) / N = ∫ t, f t ∂t`? -/
@[category research open, AMS 42]
theorem erdos_996 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (C : ℝ), 0 < C ∧ ∀ (f : Lp ℂ 2 (haarAddCircle (T := 1))) (n : ℕ → ℕ),
    IsLacunary n →
    (fun k => (eLpNorm (⇑f - fourierPartial f k) 2 (haarAddCircle (T := 1))).toReal) =O[atTop]
    (fun k => 1 / (log (log (log k))) ^ C)
    →
    ∀ᵐ x, Tendsto (fun N => (∑ k ∈ .range N, f (n k • x)) / N) atTop
    (𝓝 (∫ t, f t ∂haarAddCircle)) := by
  sorry

/-- The following theorem is proved in [Ma66]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 42]
theorem erdos_996.variants.log2 : ∀ (C : ℝ), 0.5 < C →
    ∀ (f : Lp ℂ 2 (haarAddCircle (T := 1))) (n : ℕ → ℕ),
    IsLacunary n →
    (fun k => (eLpNorm (⇑f - fourierPartial f k) 2 (haarAddCircle (T := 1))).toReal) =O[atTop]
    (fun k => 1 / (log (log k)) ^ C)
    →
    ∀ᵐ x, Tendsto (fun N => (∑ k ∈ .range N, f (n k • x)) / N) atTop
    (𝓝 (∫ t, f t ∂haarAddCircle)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos996

reformulations.difference: Erdős’s primary paper uses normalized, mean-zero, real-valued periodic functions and states its decay condition using the squared L² remainder. Lean uses arbitrary complex L² functions on ℝ/ℤ, convergence to their mean, the unsquared norm, and eventual rather than global lacunarity.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Centering changes only the zero Fourier coefficient, and normalization multiplies remainder norms by a constant absorbed by Big-O. The symmetric Fourier projection commutes with real and imaginary parts, whose remainder norms are bounded by the complex remainder norm. Applying the normalized real assertion to these components yields the complex assertion; zero-norm components are trivial. The converse follows by embedding normalized real functions into complex L². Squaring the remainder bound replaces C by 2C, preserving the existential quantifier over positive exponents. Finally, an eventually lacunary natural sequence has a positive globally lacunary tail. Removing a fixed prefix preserves Cesàro convergence: its sum divided by N tends to zero, and the tail’s relative length tends to one. Nonzero integer multiplication preserves Haar measure, so L² representatives do not affect the almost-everywhere conclusion.

reformulations.difference: Matsuyama’s corollary assumes real, mean-zero, unit-L² periodic functions and a globally lacunary sequence of positive integers. Lean removes the normalization, allows complex values, and permits an arbitrary finite prefix of the sequence.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Centering, scaling, and applying the real corollary separately to the real and imaginary components give exactly the arbitrary-complex-function statement with limit equal to the integral. Conversely, the normalized real case is included. Eventual lacunarity supplies a positive globally lacunary tail, and finite prefixes do not affect Cesàro limits. Matsuyama defines R(N) as the square root of the integral of the squared Fourier remainder, so his condition R(N)=O((log log N)^(-α)) with α>1/2 matches Lean’s norm and threshold without any exponent adjustment.

review.notes: Checked all three declarations; no mathematical defect or status discrepancy found. Successful Lean checks cover Fourier intervals at k=0,1,2, exact reproduction of included Fourier monomials, finiteness of every remainder norm, integrability of f, equality of volume and normalized Haar measure at period 1, measure preservation under nonzero integer multiplication, a lacunary witness 2^k, eventual positivity, non-vacuity of the decay hypothesis, and growth of the iterated logarithm. Full source-to-Lean equivalences were not formally proved. The live erdosproblems.com page and forum returned Cloudflare challenges despite descriptive User-Agent headers; the statement comparison uses both cited primary papers, and the community database currently records 996 as open. The reviewed file matches the specified commit.
